headline: React buys this app almost nothing that the owner's three named drivers actually require. Navigation, realtime currency and cross-device sync are solved by a state/store module (~3-4 tasks), a serializable panel registry with history integration (~4-6 tasks), and the Worker+D1 `/sync` already specified in docs/research/04a-architecture.md §7 (~8-12 tasks) — 15-22 tasks total, all in vanilla, all of which React would ALSO require us to build by hand. A big-bang React rewrite costs 85-120 tasks (8-11 CP2-programmes — more than the entire remaining product roadmap combined) and delivers zero new user-visible capability, which is precisely the "חבל על העבודה" outcome. Critically, JSX is not neutral here: I verified that acorn.parse (the engine behind scripts/i18n-extract.mjs and Guards A/D) THROWS on JSX, while htm tagged templates parse cleanly and L() call sites inside ${} are still found — so if we ever do go component-based, the path is Preact+htm inlined by build.py, never React+JSX. The genuine good news: ~47% of app.js (5,412 lines / 532 functions) is already framework-agnostic logic, and the registered appjs-modularization roadmap IS the migration path in disguise — it just needs two amendments and a rename.
recommendation:
DO NOT adopt React now. Execute this order; every item is work we need regardless of the eventual UI framework.

1. NOW, before E4 — build the STATE module (state.js/ST), ~3-4 tasks. Today state is ~30 module-level `let`s plus flat localStorage keys behind `store` (app.js:1628), and repaint is manual paintX() calls. Add a subscribe/publish bus: ST.set(k,v) notifies subscribed views. This is the single prerequisite shared by ALL THREE of the owner's drivers, and it also kills the A7 bug class ("computed but no reader" — _planSafetyViolations, app.js:6983). Framework-neutral by construction.

2. NEXT, the already-queued navigation pillar — build NAV, ~4-6 tasks. There is literally zero URL routing in 11,564 lines (verified: no pushState/popstate/hashchange/location.hash anywhere). panelStack is an array of reopener CLOSURES (app.js:3305/3335/3336); 56 open* panel functions, only 11 route through openFrom. Android hardware-back closes the PWA instead of going back one panel. The fix is a serializable panel descriptor ({panel:'cut',key:'cut-1'}) + pushState + popstate→panelBack. React Router would require the exact same serializable descriptors — the descriptors ARE the work; the router is ~100 lines either way. This is driver #1 delivered without React.

3. IN PARALLEL with E4/CP3/CP4 — keep taking modules out by attrition per docs/analysis/program/registered-2026-07-25-appjs-modularization.md. ORCH rides E2-E4, I18N rides D9. Marginal cost ~1 task per module (E1 was 5 tasks total and one of those was the F5 guard). Generalize build.py's hardcoded equipment.js block into a MODULES list at the second extraction, exactly as the roadmap already says.

4. AFTER NAV — Worker /sync + D1, per 04a §7 step 5: LWW on updatedAt, client-encrypted blobs, no CRDTs. ~8-12 tasks. Driver #3. Zero React content.

5. AMEND the modularization roadmap and re-scope it as the migration path, goal restated: not "shrink app.js" but "make the RENDER LAYER the only thing that would ever need rewriting." Two additions: (a) add STATE to the candidate table — it is missing and it is the keystone; (b) codify the render contract as a rule — every render function stays pure(state) -> html string with wiring separated (renderX/wireX, already the de facto convention across 110 innerHTML sites + 395 addEventListener sites). That convention IS the React seam; codifying it costs nothing and is what makes a future swap cheap.

6. FOR THE JUST-APPROVED WORK — make the outcome vector a DATA STRUCTURE returned by a logic function, consumed by the CP2 panel renderer. Never let outcome prose live in the renderer. rules.js emitting typed codes only (already approved) is exactly right: typed codes are renderer-independent, prose is not. Same for the wrap-trigger stage and svOrderDesc — the ORDER and the OUTCOME are logic; the sentence is render.

If a trigger fires (below), the path is (b) strangler fig with Preact+htm, one screen at a time, mounting into the same host elements the innerHTML sites already own — NOT a rewrite, NOT React+JSX.

survives.asset: The domain/logic layer — 5,412 lines across 532 functions (~47% of app.js): itemStages, effectiveSchedule, deviceOccupancy, eqmValidity, schedulePlacements, cookerContention, deviceCapacity, composedSteps, the whole cited-safety path
survives.survivesHow: Framework-agnostic already. These functions take data and return data; none touch the DOM. A UI swap does not read them differently. equipment.js/EQM (441 lines, shipped v263) is live proof the pattern works — inlined by build.py, exposes ONE narrow global, and app.js only ever CALLS EQM.*
survives.condition: Keep the extraction discipline: every new pillar leaves app.js as its own file with an F5 single-definition guard in build.py. Do NOT let new logic land inside a render function — that is exactly how buildList became a nested closure (BIG-STATUS S2, 25 gaps, 'a private closure inside a render fn')

survives.asset: The i18n system — 1,894 L() call sites, the acorn extractor (scripts/i18n-extract.mjs), and Guards A/B/C/D in build.py
survives.survivesHow: L(he,en) is a plain CallExpression with static string-literal args. The extractor's walk() is a fully generic AST traversal over every node key, so it finds L() anywhere — including inside a tagged-template's ${} expressions. VERIFIED by running acorn: the htm template parses and the nested L() site is found; JSX THROWS 'Unexpected token (1:21)'
survives.condition: HARD CONDITION: if we ever go component-based, use htm tagged templates, not JSX. JSX requires acorn-jsx in the extractor AND breaks Guard D's plain-regex pass over app.js source (build.py:453) AND would force extraction over compiled output. If someone proposes JSX, that is a spec-waiver-grade decision and must reach the owner in conversation

survives.asset: The 816-test Playwright suite, the warm-page fixture architecture, and the certified workers:20 geometry
survives.survivesHow: 66 real .click() sites, 43 [data-*] locators and ~372 document-reading evaluates are all DOM-contract assertions — they care about rendered output, not about who rendered it. The tests/_fixtures.ts warm-page + route.fulfill architecture is transport-level and framework-blind
survives.condition: 84 of 126 spec files gate on bare globals (typeof openTimeline==='function'; (window as any).resolveItem / svSmokeFinish / effectiveSchedule). app.js has ZERO top-level `window.X =` exports — those names are visible only because the whole thing is ONE non-module <script>. ANY bundler/ESM step makes them module-scoped and 84 spec files hang to timeout. Cheap to save: keep the output an IIFE and re-export the same identifier set onto window (~1 task). Register this as an explicit pre-condition on ANY build-step change, or it gets discovered the hard way

survives.asset: The single-file build model and the no-Node Cloudflare deploy path
survives.survivesHow: build.py inlines app.css + equipment.js + app.js + the Python data layer with no bundler and no JS dependencies in production (package.json has only playwright + acorn as devDeps). Preact+htm can be inlined the same way as a plain global
survives.condition: Do not introduce a bundler as a DEPLOY-time dependency. build.py:449 explicitly records that 'python build.py alone has no guaranteed Node there' — that is why Guard D exists as a regex fallback. If a bundle ever becomes necessary, pre-build and commit the artifact so deploy stays python-only

survives.asset: All CSS (1,780 lines) and the RTL/Hebrew layout work
survives.survivesHow: Class names and markup structure carry over verbatim into htm or JSX. This is the part of the render layer that genuinely does NOT die
survives.condition: Keep the S10 work (presentation tokens — type/space/radius still untokenised per BIG-STATUS S10, 19 gaps) framework-neutral: CSS custom properties, not JS-in-CSS

dies.asset: The string-concatenation render plumbing — ~6,148 lines across 203 UI functions, 110 `host.innerHTML = template` sites and 395 addEventListener wirings
dies.whyLost: A component framework replaces innerHTML = html + wireX(host) with declarative render + props. The template CONTENT survives (markup + classes + L() calls); the concat/wire scaffolding does not. Realistically 30-40% of those lines is genuine plumbing loss, not the whole 6,148
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Partly, and only if we swap incrementally. Under the strangler each panel converts on its own schedule and the ones we never convert never die. Under a big-bang rewrite ALL of it dies at once, including panels nobody has complained about

dies.asset: Per-panel visual and Hebrew evidence — DoD lines 8 and 9 re-paid for 56 panels
dies.whyLost: Every converted panel needs a fresh 390x844 screenshot, a Hebrew render check with no English leak, correct plurals on interpolated counts, and dir="ltr" islands re-verified (L13 — bidi flips >= into <=). This is the largest hidden cost of any UI rewrite and it is not optional under §3
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Only by converting incrementally, so the evidence cost is amortized across phases that were being re-verified anyway. It cannot be skipped or batched — the v267 halt and the v269/v270 'verify rendered, not the metric' lesson both came from exactly this shortcut

dies.whyLost: Closures are not serializable, so they cannot survive a reload, a URL, or a device handoff. Any router — React's or ours — requires replacing them with serializable descriptors
dies.couldWeSaveIt: No, and we should not want to. This dies in path (d) too. It IS the actual navigation work, and it is why 'React handles navigation better' is a misdiagnosis: React does not save us this refactor, it presumes we already did it

dies.asset: 'Fully interactive at DOMContentLoaded' — the property tests/_fixtures.ts relies on (dclGoto defaults every goto to 'domcontentloaded' because 'the app is a single synchronous inline script, fully interactive at DCL')
dies.whyLost: Any framework that mounts a tree after parse introduces a gap between DCL and interactive. On a 6,063,651-char document that gap is measurable
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Yes — mount islands lazily, only when a panel opens, which is already how the 56 open* panels behave. But it has to be a stated design constraint from task 1, not discovered after 84 spec files start flaking

triggers: A SECOND CLIENT WITH A DIFFERENT LAYOUT — a real desktop/PC surface that is not just 'the mobile UI at 1440px', or a partner embed. Component reuse across two genuinely different layouts is React's strongest real win and we do not have that case today.

A COLLABORATIVE SURFACE — two HUMANS editing the same cookout at the same time (owner + helper at the fire), not one user on N devices. That is when concurrent updates hit many small components and hand-written repaint becomes a bug factory. 04a §4 is right that single-user-multi-device needs only LWW blobs and no CRDTs — that case does NOT trigger a framework change.

THE EMPIRICAL REPAINT TRIGGER — after the STATE module ships, measure it: if more than ~30% of new defects are 'the view did not update' or 'two views disagree', declarative rendering is earning its keep and we start the strangler. If they are not, we have our answer.

A SECOND DEVELOPER JOINS who is React-fluent, and teaching the vanilla render/wire conventions demonstrably costs more than the incremental migration. This is the most likely trigger in practice and it is a legitimate one.

BUILD STEP FORCED FROM OUTSIDE — if some other requirement (TypeScript, a large dependency, code-splitting the 6MB payload) makes a bundler unavoidable anyway, the marginal cost of a component layer drops sharply and the calculus should be redone.
ANTI-TRIGGER, stated out loud: 'app.js is getting big' is NOT a trigger. That is what the attrition roadmap is for, and it is already working.

risks.risk: JSX silently disables the i18n guard chain. scripts/i18n-extract.mjs calls acorn.parse(src,{ecmaVersion:2022,sourceType:'script'}) — I ran it against JSX and it throws 'Unexpected token (1:21)'. Guard A (coverage), Guard D (call-site signature) and the suite's extractor-re-run gate all sit downstream. A broken extractor means untranslated strings ship to 23 languages with the build still green.
risks.mitigation: Use htm tagged templates — VERIFIED to parse under the existing acorn config with the nested L() CallExpression still discoverable. If JSX is ever proposed anyway, treat it as a §4 waiver-gate item: it must reach the owner in conversation, and the first task must be a RED test proving the extractor still finds every L() site.

risks.risk: 84 of 126 spec files (67%) boot-gate on app.js functions being bare globals (typeof openTimeline==='function'). app.js exports ZERO names to window explicitly — the visibility is an accident of being one non-module <script>. Any ESM/bundle step turns 84 spec files into 30s timeouts, which will read as 'the migration broke everything'.
risks.mitigation: Cheap and known: emit an IIFE and re-export the same identifier set onto window as an explicit, build-guarded contract (the same F5 pattern equipment.js uses for EQM). ~1 task. Do it as the FIRST task of any build-step change, never as cleanup afterwards.

risks.risk: Two rendering systems coexisting over one DOM for months — the exact failure shape the localization arc just spent v268-v277 unwinding (BIG-STATUS S7: 'two competing translation mechanisms over one DOM', 11 gaps). A React island and a vanilla paintX() both owning a subtree will produce the same class of ghost bugs.
risks.mitigation: Strangler rule: a DOM subtree has exactly ONE owner, declared. Convert whole panels, never halves. Add a test asserting no converted host is also written by an innerHTML site. This repo has already paid for this mistake once — do not pay twice.

risks.risk: A bundler becomes a deploy-time Node dependency, breaking the Cloudflare path. build.py:449 explicitly records that 'python build.py alone has no guaranteed Node there' — that constraint is why Guard D exists as a regex fallback at all.
risks.mitigation: Preact+htm needs no build step: inline the runtime as a global via build.py's existing module-inlining slot. If a bundler ever becomes necessary, pre-build and commit the artifact so deploy stays python-only.

risks.risk: Hydration/mount cost on a 6,063,651-char document (DATA begins at char 224,855 — the payload is ~96% data, ~4% code). Mounting a component tree over 56 panels changes the DCL-interactive property the whole test fixture assumes.
risks.mitigation: Mount per-panel on open, never eagerly — which is already how the app behaves. Note the corollary honestly: React+ReactDOM at ~45KB gzip is ~0.7% of this payload, so 'bundle size on mobile' is NOT a valid argument against a framework here. The 5.8MB data payload is the real perf problem and it is framework-independent.

risks.risk: The React question delays the server work. Cross-device sync is 100% server and 0% React, but 'we should decide the framework first' is a very natural way to stall it — and it is the driver with real product value.
risks.mitigation: Sequence sync BEFORE any framework decision and make that explicit. It also carries genuinely new surface: auth, entitlement, and PII under Israeli PPL Amendment 13 / GDPR (04a §4) — opt-in, client-encrypted, with export/delete.

risks.risk: Scope creep dressed as migration. 'While we are in here' rewrites of panels nobody asked about — the §12 Circle-of-Control failure mode. A migration is the single most fertile ground for it.
risks.mitigation: Attrition rule from the registered roadmap, enforced: a pillar is extracted/converted only when a programme phase re-architects it. Idle refactoring is not approved work. Opportunistic extraction only at a phase boundary, with owner sign-off.

effort:
UNIT CALIBRATION, measured from this repo's own plans: CP2 = 11 tasks (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-cooking-paths-cp2.md); E1 = 5 tasks and shipped equipment.js (441 lines) + 356 test lines + call-site rewiring + the build.py F5 guard. So 1 task ~= ~90 lines of shipped module code + ~70 lines of test + a full DoD cycle (RED witnessed, GREEN, 390x844 screenshot, Hebrew check, full suite). All figures below are in those tasks; 11 tasks = 1 CP2.

(a) BIG-BANG REWRITE — 85-120 tasks (8-11 CP2s). NOT ACCEPTABLE.
- UI layer: 6,148 lines / 203 UI functions / 56 panels. Rewriting is not cheaper than writing — every panel still owes DoD-8 (screenshot) and DoD-9 (Hebrew, plurals, dir=ltr islands). ~65-70 tasks.
- Test harness: ~1 task if we keep an IIFE with global re-exports; 25-40 tasks if we genuinely rewrite to component tests.
- Build/i18n pipeline: htm route ~2 tasks; JSX route ~4-6 (acorn-jsx + Guard D re-anchoring + extractor re-validation).
- Server/D1/sync: 8-12 tasks (auth, entitlement, schema, protocol, conflict, offline queue, migration, tests).
- REALITY CHECK: the ENTIRE remaining product roadmap — E4, CP3, CP4, E5/E6, P0-worker, P3, P4, P5a, P5b, P7, P8 solver — is roughly 60-90 tasks. The rewrite costs more than everything left to build and ships no feature. This is the owner's fear made literal.

(b) STRANGLER FIG (Preact+htm) — 48-64 tasks total, but INCREMENTAL and pausable.
- Seam: STATE store+bus (3-4) + inline the runtime in build.py with an F5 guard (1) + test-global bridge (1) + one-owner-per-subtree assertion (1) = 6-8 tasks.
- Then ~0.75-1 task per panel x 56 panels = ~40-56 tasks, each independently shippable, each stoppable.
- The seam is unusually clean: host.innerHTML = renderX(state) + wireX(host) maps almost mechanically to render(html`...`, host). The blockers are (i) no central store — that IS the STATE module, needed anyway; (ii) two module systems in one file — solved by the equipment.js inlining pattern; (iii) JSX vs htm — verified above.
- Never pay this all at once. Pay it only when a trigger fires, panel by panel.

(c) LOGIC-FIRST EXTRACTION — ~5-6 tasks MARGINAL. RECOMMENDED, and mostly already funded.
- ORCH, NAV, VOICE, AI, I18N each ride the phase that re-architects them (E2-E4, the nav pillar, the voice track, post-E5 AI work, D9). E1 proved the shape at 5 tasks; the marginal cost of taking the module out DURING a phase is ~1 task each, because the seam test and the F5 guard are the only additions.
- Plus the missing keystone: STATE, 3-4 tasks, which I recommend funding explicitly rather than letting it ride.

(d) STAY VANILLA AND SOLVE THE THREE DRIVERS — 15-22 tasks. THIS IS THE ANSWER.
- Navigation (driver #1): serializable panel registry + pushState/popstate = 4-6 tasks. React saves us none of this.
- Realtime currency (driver #2): STATE store+bus, subscribed repaint = 3-4 tasks. Also closes the A7 'computed but never surfaced' bug class.
- Cross-device/PC sync (driver #3): Worker /sync + D1, LWW on updatedAt, client-encrypted blobs = 8-12 tasks. Zero React content; 04a §2b/§4/§7 already specifies it.

BOTTOM LINE IN ONE LINE: 15-22 tasks delivers all three of the owner's drivers in vanilla; 85-120 tasks delivers none of them and throws away the render layer.
openQuestions: What does 'עדכניות realtime' mean CONCRETELY? (a) the live cook timeline ticking and the plan recomputing after an edit — already works via manual paintX(), the gap is only views that fail to repaint; or (b) 'my phone shows within seconds what I changed on the PC' — that is push/polling from the Worker, a different build. Different costs, and only (b) needs the server.

Is the multi-device case ever TWO PEOPLE at once (owner + helper at the same cookout), or always one person across N devices? This single answer decides LWW-blobs vs real reconciliation, AND it is the strongest determinant of whether a declarative framework earns its keep. 04a §4 assumed single-user; if that assumption is now wrong, 04a needs re-opening.

Is a PC/desktop layout a genuinely DIFFERENT layout, or just the mobile UI on a bigger screen? A real second layout is the best React argument that exists for this app; 'responsive mobile at 1440px' is not.
Will a second developer join in the next 12 months? That changes the calculus more than any technical factor here — better said now than discovered mid-phase.

Should docs/analysis/program/registered-2026-07-25-appjs-modularization.md be formally RENAMED and re-scoped as 'the migration-readiness roadmap', with STATE added to the candidate table and the pure-render contract codified? That is a change to a registered work item, so I am treating it as an owner call rather than a routine one.

Does 'client/server' in the owner's framing mean anything beyond sync + the managed-AI proxy we already run? Specifically: does he want server-side RENDERING, or server-side RULES? The latter would contradict the settled decision that the rules engine and all safety values stay client-side and cited — worth confirming explicitly before anyone plans around it.
